prerequisites: A category is a set of objects with a stated property.
Understand every, none, at least one and not.
explanation: Translate the statement before drawing a diagram. All A are B forbids an A outside B. No A are B forbids overlap. Some A are B requires at least one shared witness. Some A are not B requires at least one A outside B. In this unit, universal statements do not assert that a category exists. Some means at least one, not some but not all. Use only the stated categories, not real-world beliefs.

worked.action: All badges are blue: any object that is a badge must belong to blue things. The blue set may also contain objects that are not badges.
worked.justification: Containment is directional. This does not say all blue things are badges or that badges exist.

worked.action: No badges are round: the badge/round overlap is forbidden.
worked.justification: An empty overlap can be described in either direction, but neither category is required to contain a witness.

worked.action: Some badges are blue: put one witness in both sets.
worked.justification: At least one witness is guaranteed. Additional witnesses and full containment are neither required nor excluded.

worked.action: Some badges are not round: put a badge witness outside the round set.
worked.justification: This is a positive existence claim with a negative membership condition. It does not say no badges are round.

worked.action: Only trained staff may supervise means all supervisors are trained staff.
worked.justification: Only introduces a necessary condition: being a supervisor requires training. It does not make every trained person a supervisor.

worked.action: Not every report is signed means some report is not signed.
worked.justification: Negating a universal supplies a counterexample. With no reports at all, every report is signed would be vacuously true, so its negation cannot hold.

hint: Identify the subject category, the condition, and whether a witness is asserted or a region forbidden.
shortcut: Mark all/no as forbidden-region constraints and some/some-not as required-witness constraints.
limitation: This explicit no-existential-import convention applies to these authored checks. Follow any different existence assumptions stated in an exam question.
